verification_scope: the force attribute on APP_ENV, which was already verified, PLUS the eight keys the suite depended on but never declared - the Recommended Improvement's remaining half, and the reason this entry was held at mitigated. All eight are now in the tracked <php> block of api/phpunit.xml: COMPANY_SALES_INBOX_EMAIL, COMPANY_CERTIFICATION, COMPANY_LOGO_PATH, COMPANY_EMAIL_BRAND_NAME, ACCOUNTING_FUNCTIONAL_CURRENCY_CODE, ADMIN_NAME, ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PASSWORD, each with a comment naming its consumer. None is forced: the attribute stays on APP_ENV and that entry only, because forcing an entry lets this file outrank CI's job-scoped env, which is the defect this entry already documents for DB_HOST, DB_DATABASE and DB_PASSWORD. Values are derived from the code's own fallbacks rather than chosen: EmailBrandingService::data() for the COMPANY_* keys, the literal migration 0358 inserts for the sales inbox, the literal migration 0309 inserts for the functional currency, and empty for COMPANY_LOGO_PATH because that is migration 0123's default and api/.env.example's value and no template renders company.logo_path. NOT claimed, and stated plainly in the Status note: the suite asserts none of these eight values, and the three ADMIN_* keys are not exercised by it at all, since AdminUserSeeder is reachable only through DatabaseSeeder and no test seeds DatabaseSeeder. What is verified is the Ideal Process itself - the suite's declared configuration is the configuration it runs in, and it no longer varies with an untracked file. SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-19: as written on 2026-08-18 that last clause was overstated, because the list of eight was itself incomplete. The key list was re-derived mechanically rather than trusted - every env(), $envString() and $envFloat() key under api/database/seeders and api/database/migrations, 22 distinct keys, diffed against the names declared in api/phpunit.xml - and five were still undeclared: COMPANY_EMPLOYEE_EMAIL_DOMAIN, COMPANY_LATITUDE, COMPANY_LONGITUDE, QUALITY_COC_MANAGER_NAME and QUALITY_COC_MANAGER_ROLE. All five are SettingsSeeder rows sitting in its $deploymentKeys list, where a blank env value skips the write but a non-blank one overwrites the migration's row for the whole suite - the same mechanism the eight closed. All five are now declared, so the claim holds for the whole configuration rather than for eight keys: re-running the derivation afterwards returns an empty set. Values are migration 0308's literal for the email domain and migration 0442's literals for the two coordinates; the two QUALITY_COC_MANAGER keys are declared EMPTY because no migration seeds either (both rows are absent after a full migrate), CoCService:138,139 falls back to the empty string, api/.env.example leaves both blank, and coc.blade.php:147,148 already substitutes a dash and Quality Management - a fabricated name would sign every certificate of conformance the suite renders with a fictitious human. force=true remains on APP_ENV and that entry alone; none of the five is forced. Also retracted in the register on the same date, as a self-contradiction rather than a new fact: the Recommended Improvement's sentence that genuine env-file isolation needs a committed testing env file carrying the COMPANY_* and ADMIN_* keys. A phpunit.xml <env> entry is applied before Laravel's LoadEnvironmentVariables bootstrapper and Laravel's Dotenv is immutable, so a declared key outranks ANY loaded env file. Declaring keys in the tracked block is therefore strictly stronger than committing a .env.testing - which would itself lose to that block - and needs no new tracked file. api/phpunit.xml:52-57 already stated this precedence and the finding never did, which is how the two came to disagree while this row read verified.
